answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive by requiring every new agent to lock a bond in a bridge contract before receiving jobs. Existing agents issue lotus challenge tasks, and anyone can expose copied or colluding identities; a successful proof slashes the bond and pays the reporter. Legitimate work unlocks the bond over time, while a Sybil attacker must fund each fabricated identity separately and risks losing every bond, making fake-agent scaling a recurring capital cost rather than free account creation in a haven.
